title: L‐glutamate‐stimulated taurine release from rat cerebral cultured astrocytes

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We characterized L‐glutamate‐stimulated taurine release from cultured astrocytes prepared from rat cerebrum. L‐glutamate (0.5 mM) stimulated release of <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐labeled and endogenous taurine, where the rate of release reached maximum in 40 min. L‐glutamate increased astrocytic volume [<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐O‐methyl‐D‐glucose (<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐OMG) space] with a similar time course to <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐taurine release. Quisqualate, L‐aspartate, DL‐homocysteate, and L‐cysteate increased both astrocytic <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐OMG space and <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐taurine release from cultured astrocytes, while kainate (1 mM) stimulated <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐taurine release without affecting astrocytic volume. N‐methyl‐D‐aspartate had no effect on <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐taurine release and astrocytic volume. Treatment of astrocytes with dibutyryl cAMP reduced the effect of kainate on <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐taurine release. L‐glutamate‐stimulated <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐taurine release was attenuated by removal of extracellular Cl<jats:sup>−</jats:sup> and in hyperosmotic medium, which prevented L‐glutamate‐induced increase in <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>H‐OMG space of cultured astrocytes. These results indicate that L‐glutamate stimulates taurine release from astrocytes through swelling‐triggered mechanisms and that kainate causes the release through volume‐independent mechanisms. © 1994 Wiley‐Liss, Inc.</jats:p>
